title: India–Indonesia Defence Deal: BrahMos and Astra Missiles to Be Supplied to Indonesia
summary: India is set to supply BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles and Astra air-to-air missiles to Indonesia, confirmed by an Indian government official during PM Modi's state visit to Jakarta. This marks a significant expansion of India's defence exports under its 'Make in India' and defence export push. The deal is part of a broader strategic partnership being formalised between the two countries. Indonesia becomes one of the key Southeast Asian nations to acquire the BrahMos system, which is jointly developed by India and Russia.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR/Defence) — India's defence export ambitions, BrahMos as a strategic product, and deepening ties with ASEAN nations under Act East Policy.
key_facts: Missiles: BrahMos (supersonic cruise) and Astra (air-to-air)
BrahMos is a joint venture between India (DRDO/BrahMos Aerospace) and Russia
Indonesia is an ASEAN nation; deal part of India's Act East Policy
Announced during PM Modi's state visit to Jakarta (July 2026)

title: PM Modi Visits Indonesia: IIM Campus, UPI, AI, Critical Minerals and EVM Cooperation Announced
summary: PM Narendra Modi visited Jakarta, Indonesia, heralding what he called a 'golden chapter' in India–Indonesia relations. Key announcements included setting up an IIM Bangalore campus in Indonesia, extending UPI payment infrastructure, cooperation on artificial intelligence and critical minerals, and an MoU on election management including export of customised Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs). PM Modi also received Indonesia's highest civilian honour, the 'Bintang Adipurna'. PM Modi highlighted the next 25 years as crucial for the bilateral partnership and the Indian Ocean region.
exam_angle: Tests knowledge of India's bilateral diplomacy, Act East Policy, defence/tech exports, and India's soft power through institutions like IIMs. The EVM export MoU is significant for polity questions.
key_facts: Award received: 'Bintang Adipurna' — Indonesia's highest state honour
IIM Bangalore to set up campus in Indonesia
MoU on election management and export of customised EVMs signed
Cooperation areas: UPI, AI, critical minerals, satellite launch capability, defence
source: The Times of India / News18 / NDTV

title: PM Modi Offers Indonesia Satellite Launch Capability; Deepens Space Partnership
summary: During PM Modi's visit to Jakarta, India offered Indonesia satellite launch capability as part of deepening the bilateral space partnership. This aligns with ISRO's expanding commercial launch services under NewSpace India Limited (NSIL). The offer reflects India's growing role as a provider of space services to developing and partner nations in the Indo-Pacific region. Space cooperation was among multiple high-tech areas announced during the summit.
exam_angle: Links to ISRO's commercial arm NSIL, India's space diplomacy, and the broader theme of India as a space-faring nation offering services to allies.
key_facts: India offered satellite launch capability to Indonesia
ISRO's commercial arm: NewSpace India Limited (NSIL)
Part of India–Indonesia summit outcomes, July 2026
Relevant to India's Act East Policy and space diplomacy

title: India Urges US to Reconsider Proposed 12.5% Tariff Under USTR Section 301 'Forced Labour' Probe
summary: India has formally urged the United States to reconsider a proposed 12.5% tariff on Indian goods being examined under a Section 301 investigation by the US Trade Representative (USTR) related to 'forced labour' allegations. This is a significant trade friction point between the two countries as India seeks to protect its export competitiveness in the US market. Section 301 of the US Trade Act allows the USTR to investigate and impose tariffs on countries engaging in unfair trade practices. India's pushback comes amid broader India-US trade negotiations.
exam_angle: Tests knowledge of US trade law mechanisms (Section 301), India-US trade relations, and WTO/tariff dispute frameworks relevant to GS Paper 3 (Economy/IR).
key_facts: Tariff proposed: 12.5% on certain Indian goods
Investigation authority: USTR under Section 301 of US Trade Act
Basis of probe: 'Forced labour' allegations
India has formally requested reconsideration of the tariff

title: 2008 Ahmedabad Serial Blasts Case: Gujarat High Court Upholds Death Penalty for 38 Convicts
summary: The Gujarat High Court upheld the death penalty for 38 convicts in the 2008 Ahmedabad serial blasts case, which involved a series of bomb explosions across the city that killed over 56 people and injured hundreds. The government described the verdict as a 'historic victory'. The case involved one of the largest terrorist attacks in India and the trial court had earlier awarded the death sentence to 38 and life imprisonment to others. The High Court confirmation is a necessary step before the matter can go to the Supreme Court.
exam_angle: Relevant to criminal law, capital punishment jurisprudence, and constitutional provisions on the right to life (Article 21). Also tests knowledge of India's counter-terrorism legal framework.
key_facts: Incident: 2008 Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts (56+ killed)
Court: Gujarat High Court upheld death penalty
Number of convicts on death row confirmed: 38
Mandatory confirmation of death sentences by High Court under CrPC before Supreme Court appeal

title: E20 Petrol Row: Supreme Court Takes Up Petition; Concerns Over Damage to E10 Vehicles
summary: A report and a Supreme Court petition have raised concerns that E20 petrol (containing 20% ethanol blended with petrol) may damage rubber fuel system components in older vehicles designed for E10 (10% ethanol blend). A litigant before the Supreme Court alleged 'silent compulsion' in the E20 rollout. India is pursuing its ethanol blending programme — achieving 20% blending by 2025–26 — as part of its energy security and climate commitments. Petroleum Minister Hardeep Puri defended the programme, saying car manufacturers are comfortable with the transition.
exam_angle: Connects to India's National Biofuel Policy, ethanol blending targets, energy security, and the intersection of environmental policy with consumer rights.
key_facts: E20 = 20% ethanol blended petrol; E10 = 10% ethanol blend
India's target: 20% ethanol blending by 2025–26 under National Biofuel Policy 2018
Concern: E20 may damage rubber parts in E10-compatible vehicles
Matter raised before the Supreme Court of India

title: Wayanad Landslide: IMD Red Alert, 5 Dead; Kerala Ministers Term It 'Man-Made Disaster'
summary: A landslide struck Wayanad district in Kerala following heavy rainfall, killing at least 5 people and prompting a red alert from the India Meteorological Department (IMD). Two Kerala ministers termed the disaster 'man-made', raising questions about construction activity and deforestation in the ecologically sensitive Western Ghats. Wayanad was the site of a catastrophic landslide in July 2024 as well, making it a region of recurring disaster vulnerability. Simultaneously, the IMD issued red alerts for Delhi and an orange alert for Mumbai as the monsoon intensified across India.
exam_angle: Relevant to disaster management, Western Ghats ecology, Gadgil and Kasturirangan Committee recommendations on ecologically sensitive zones, and IMD's alert system.
key_facts: Location: Wayanad, Kerala — ecologically sensitive part of Western Ghats
Deaths: At least 5 in the latest landslide
IMD alert levels: Red (extreme), Orange (very heavy), Yellow (heavy rainfall) — colour-coded system
Kerala ministers attributed the disaster to human activity ('man-made')

title: Strait of Hormuz Tanker Attacks: Three Commercial Ships Hit, Oil Prices Rise
summary: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that three commercial tankers were hit by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz, with no casualties reported. Oil prices rose on reports of the attack, which was attributed to Iranian-linked activity by media reports. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints, through which roughly 20% of global oil trade passes. The attacks are part of ongoing escalation in the West Asia/Middle East region.
exam_angle: Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global energy security and directly impacts India's oil import costs. Relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy — energy security).
key_facts: Location: Strait of Hormuz — between Iran and Oman
~20% of global oil trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz
Reporting authority: UKMTO (UK Maritime Trade Operations)
Three tankers hit; oil prices rose on news of attacks

title: Macron Visits Syria: Blast Near Damascus Hotel During French Presidential Visit
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron made a state visit to Damascus, Syria — a significant diplomatic visit marking engagement with Syria's new post-Assad government. During the visit, a blast was reported near his hotel, though Macron was unharmed. The visit signalled Western re-engagement with Syria following the fall of Bashar al-Assad's government. France's diplomatic outreach to Syria is part of broader international efforts to stabilise the country and address the refugee and humanitarian crisis.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR) — geopolitics of West Asia, France's foreign policy, and Syria's post-conflict political transition.
key_facts: French President Macron visited Damascus, Syria
Blast reported near his hotel during the visit; Macron was unharmed
Significance: Western diplomatic re-engagement with post-Assad Syria
Syria's Assad government fell in late 2024 after rebel offensive

title: UNICEF: Over 300 Children Killed or Wounded in Sudan War in Six Months
summary: UNICEF reported that over 300 children have been killed or wounded in Sudan's ongoing civil war over a period of six months, highlighting the severe humanitarian toll of the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The Sudan conflict, which began in April 2023, has created one of the world's largest displacement crises. UNICEF's report underscores the violation of international humanitarian law and the targeting of civilian infrastructure in the war.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR) — international organisations (UNICEF), humanitarian law, and Africa-related current affairs that frequently appear in UPSC Prelims.
key_facts: 300+ children killed or wounded in Sudan conflict over 6 months: UNICEF
Sudan conflict: SAF vs RSF (Rapid Support Forces), began April 2023
One of the world's largest displacement/humanitarian crises
UNICEF is a UN agency focused on children's welfare (HQ: New York)

title: Trump Considers Selling F-35 Fighter Jets to Turkey
summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the United States would consider selling F-35 stealth fighter jets to Turkey. Turkey was originally part of the F-35 programme but was removed in 2019 after it purchased Russia's S-400 air defence system, triggering US sanctions under CAATSA (Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act). Trump's statement signals a possible shift in US policy and a potential easing of tensions with Turkey, a NATO ally. The development is significant for NATO cohesion and US arms export policy.
exam_angle: Connects to CAATSA (relevant because India also purchased S-400 from Russia), NATO dynamics, and US arms export policy — all frequent UPSC IR themes.
key_facts: F-35 is a 5th-generation stealth multirole fighter (Lockheed Martin)
Turkey was expelled from F-35 programme in 2019 after S-400 purchase from Russia
CAATSA (Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act) was the sanctions basis
India also purchased S-400 from Russia and faced CAATSA waiver pressure

title: Ukraine Strikes 8 Russian 'Shadow Fleet' Tankers Delivering Fuel to Crimea
summary: Ukraine conducted strikes on eight Russian 'shadow fleet' tankers that were delivering fuel to Crimea, which Russia annexed in 2014. The 'shadow fleet' refers to vessels used by Russia to circumvent Western oil sanctions imposed after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Targeting of these tankers represents Ukraine's strategy to disrupt Russian fuel supply lines, especially to occupied territories. The development has implications for global shipping insurance and maritime security.
exam_angle: Relevant to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, Western sanctions architecture, the concept of 'shadow fleets', and energy security — all important for GS Paper 2 IR and GS Paper 3 Economy.
key_facts: 'Shadow fleet': vessels used to evade Western oil sanctions on Russia
Crimea was annexed by Russia in 2014; internationally recognised as Ukrainian territory
Eight tankers struck by Ukraine in this operation
Western sanctions cap Russian oil at $60/barrel under G7 Price Cap mechanism

title: TribeX Digital Learning Platform for Tribal Arts and Culture Launched by Union Tribal Affairs Minister
summary: Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Jual Oram launched 'TribeX', a digital learning platform dedicated to tribal arts, culture, and traditional knowledge. The platform is designed to preserve, promote, and disseminate India's rich tribal heritage in a digital format, making it accessible to tribal communities and the wider public. The launch aligns with the Ministry of Tribal Affairs' mandate to protect tribal identities and livelihoods under constitutional provisions (Articles 15, 16, 46, and the Fifth and Sixth Schedules).
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (Schemes/Welfare) — government initiatives for tribal welfare, digital empowerment, and constitutional safeguards for Scheduled Tribes.
key_facts: Platform name: TribeX
Launched by: Union Minister Jual Oram, Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Purpose: Digital learning for tribal arts, culture, and traditional knowledge
Relevant constitutional provisions: Articles 46, Fifth Schedule, Sixth Schedule (NE India)

title: Taj Mahal–Tejo Mahalaya Petition: Allahabad High Court Issues Notice to Centre
summary: The Allahabad High Court issued a notice to the Central Government on a petition claiming that the Taj Mahal was built on a pre-existing Hindu temple site called 'Tejo Mahalaya'. The petition seeks a court-directed investigation into the historical claims. The Taj Mahal, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the 17th century in Agra, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of India's most iconic monuments. Similar petitions in the past have been dismissed by courts.
exam_angle: Relevant to heritage/culture questions, Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act 1991, and constitutional provisions on religious sites — a recurring issue in UPSC current affairs.
key_facts: Monument: Taj Mahal, Agra — UNESCO World Heritage Site (designated 1983)
Built by: Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan (17th century) in memory of Mumtaz Mahal
Petition claims: Taj Mahal built over 'Tejo Mahalaya' Hindu temple site
Court: Allahabad High Court issued notice to Centre

title: ZEE5 Removes 'Satluj' (Punjab 95) After Government Cites IT Rules and Security Concerns
summary: OTT platform ZEE5 removed the film 'Satluj' (based on the Diljit Dosanjh-produced 'Punjab 95', depicting the human rights situation during the 1984–95 Punjab militancy period) after the government cited security concerns and the IT Rules 2021 as grounds for the takedown. The film had previously been held up by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). SGPC and Shiromani Akali Dal condemned the removal. The case raises questions about OTT regulation, freedom of expression, and government powers under the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules 2021.
exam_angle: Directly relevant to GS Paper 2 (Polity) — OTT regulation under IT Rules 2021, CBFC's powers, freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)), and reasonable restrictions.
key_facts: Film: 'Satluj' (Punjab 95) — depicts 1984–95 Punjab militancy and human rights issues
Platform: ZEE5 removed the film citing government direction
Legal basis cited: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules 2021
Regulatory body: CBFC (Central Board of Film Certification) had earlier withheld certification

title: Pakistan Issues 'War' Threat Over Indus Waters Amid Suspended Treaty
summary: Pakistan issued statements threatening war with India over Indus Waters, amid the monsoon season when river flows are high and following India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) after the Pahalgam terrorist attack in April 2025. India suspended the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty — brokered by the World Bank — as a retaliatory measure. The IWT governs the sharing of six rivers of the Indus system between India and Pakistan, with the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) allocated to Pakistan and eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India.
exam_angle: Critical for GS Paper 2 (IR) — Indus Waters Treaty, India–Pakistan relations, water diplomacy, and World Bank's role as a mediator/guarantor.
key_facts: Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) signed in 1960 — brokered by World Bank
Western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) allocated to Pakistan; Eastern (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India
India suspended IWT after Pahalgam terror attack (April 2025)
Pakistan threatened war over Indian actions on Indus water flows

title: Bengaluru Startup's Surveillance Satellite Knocked Out by Solar Activity
summary: A surveillance satellite operated by a Bengaluru-based startup was knocked out of service due to intense solar activity (likely a geomagnetic storm or solar flare), with the company vowing to make a comeback. The incident highlights the vulnerability of low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to space weather events. India's private space sector has been growing rapidly following the liberalisation of the space sector through the Indian Space Policy 2023 and the establishment of IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre).
exam_angle: Relevant to India's private space sector, IN-SPACe, space weather hazards, and the broader theme of space security and satellite vulnerability.
key_facts: Incident: Solar activity (geomagnetic storm/solar flare) disabled a surveillance satellite
Operator: Bengaluru-based private space startup
Regulatory body for Indian private space sector: IN-SPACe (under DoS)
Indian Space Policy 2023 opened space sector to private players

title: India's Semiconductor (Chip) Manufacturing Push Faces Execution Challenges
summary: An analysis highlights that India's semiconductor manufacturing ambitions face the biggest challenge not in policy design but in execution — including lack of specialised talent, supply chain gaps, water and power requirements, and delays in facility construction. India has approved semiconductor projects under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), including facilities by Tata Electronics (in Dholera, Gujarat) and Micron Technology (ATMP facility in Sanand, Gujarat). The global chip race is intensifying with the US CHIPS Act and EU Chips Act offering competing incentives.
exam_angle: Directly relevant to GS Paper 3 (Economy/Sci-Tech) — India Semiconductor Mission, Atmanirbhar Bharat in electronics, and critical technology supply chains.
key_facts: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched under MeitY with Rs 76,000 crore incentive package
Approved projects: Tata Electronics (Dholera, Gujarat) and Micron Technology ATMP (Sanand, Gujarat)
Key challenge highlighted: Execution — talent, supply chain, infrastructure
Global context: US CHIPS Act ($52 bn) and EU Chips Act competing for semiconductor investment
